text:
PhD Position in Economics – University f La Laguna, Spain

One funded four-year predoctoral research position (FPI / AEI)
Expected official application call: Early 2027
Expected starting date: Mid to Late 2027
 
The University of La Laguna (ULL), Tenerife, Spain, invites expressions of interest from highly motivated candidates wishing to pursue a PhD in Economics within the research project Inequality and Policy (INEQPOL), funded by the Spanish State Research Agency (AEI).

The position is associated with project PID2025-169915NB-C51, led by Prof. Gustavo A. Marrero and Prof. Carlos G. Bethencourt, and benefits from a dedicated four-year predoctoral research contract (FPI) awarded in connection with the project.

Research Environment and Project

INEQPOL is a coordinated research initiative involving five Spanish universities (University of La Laguna, Autonomous University of Barcelona, University of Vigo,
University of Girona, and Complutense University of Madrid), together with an extensive network of international collaborators.

The project investigates the determinants and consequences of economic inequality, as well as the role of public policies in shaping economic and social outcomes.

Its research agenda encompasses several interconnected areas:
 
Income and wealth inequality, redistribution, and public economics.
Inequality of opportunity, technological change, and artificial intelligence.
Education, human capital, productivity, and economic development.
Gender inequality, family economics, and labour markets.
Health economics, climate change, and environmental vulnerability.
Research within INEQPOL combines economic theory, quantitative modelling, applied econometrics, causal inference, and data-intensive empirical analysis.

The successful candidate will develop doctoral research aligned with one or more of these areas, taking into account their academic background, research interests, and the objectives of the project.

Candidate Profile
We seek academically strong and highly motivated candidates with a solid foundation in economics and quantitative methods, and a clear interest in pursuing an academic research career.

Essential qualifications:
A strong background in macroeconomic theory and microeconomic theory.
Solid training in mathematics, statistics, econometrics, and quantitative methods.
A degree in Economics or a closely related discipline, preferably complemented by postgraduate training in Economics.
A genuine interest in at least one of the research areas covered by INEQPOL.
Strong analytical skills, intellectual curiosity, and the motivation to undertake independent research.
A good command of written and spoken English.
Additional qualifications that will be valued:
Advanced coursework in economic theory, econometrics, or quantitative economics.
Experience with statistical or computational tools such as Stata, R, Python, or MATLAB.
Previous research experience, including a Master's thesis or research assistantship.

We welcome candidates with interests in theoretical, empirical, or quantitative economic research. Previous academic publications are not required.
Applicants must meet the eligibility requirements for admission to doctoral studies and for a predoctoral research contract under Spanish regulations. In particular, candidates must hold, or be in a position to obtain before enrolment, the academic qualifications required for admission to a PhD programme in Spain.

What We Offer
 A funded four-year, full-time predoctoral research contract (FPI), subject to the applicable regulations.
An indicative gross annual salary of approximately €23,000–€26,000, subject to the applicable salary scales and regulations of the University of
La Laguna.
Additional funding of up to €7,000 over the contract period to support research stays at national or international institutions and doctoral tuition
fees, in accordance with the applicable funding rules.
The possibility of a postdoctoral orientation period within the four-year contract, subject to successful completion of the PhD and the applicable
regulations.
The opportunity to pursue a PhD in Economics at the University of La Laguna, potentially under an international joint-supervision (cotutelle) agreement
with another university, subject to institutional approval.
Research supervision and mentoring by experienced academics.
Integration into a collaborative research environment with strong international connections.
Opportunities to participate in research seminars, workshops, and international conferences.
Opportunities for research collaboration and academic mobility within the INEQPOL network.
An intellectually stimulating academic environment in Tenerife, Canary Islands, Spain.

Application and Selection
Interested candidates are invited to submit an expression of interest in English, including:
 
A curriculum vitae.
Academic transcripts (undergraduate and postgraduate, where applicable).
A brief statement of motivation and research interests (maximum two pages).
A Master's thesis, research paper, or other sample of academic work, if available.
Contact information for two academic referees.
Expected date of the official application call: Early 2027 (tentative, subject to the University of La Laguna's recruitment timetable).
Expected starting date: Mid to Late 2027 (tentative, subject to completion of the official selection procedure and any necessary administrative formalities).
Deadline for expressions of interest: December 31st, 2026

Contact: gmarrero@ull.edu.es, cbethenc@ull.edu.es

Selection will be based on academic merit, strength of theoretical and quantitative training, research potential, and alignment with the project's research agenda.
The position will be filled through an open and competitive recruitment process conducted in accordance with the official procedures of the University of La Laguna. Expressions of interest do not replace the formal application required once the official call is published.
This preliminary call is intended to identify prospective candidates and facilitate early communication with the research team. It does not constitute an official job offer or guarantee selection.
Applications from suitably qualified candidates worldwide are welcome.
We would be grateful if colleagues could share this opportunity with promising students and prospective PhD candidates.
